classifications.reason: This generic breadcrumb wrapper contains the actual Home hyperlink as a distinct child. The wrapper itself has no supported or tentative action basis, so it should be treated as a container while the child link remains independently discoverable and reviewable.
evidence: The complete, untruncated classification subtree contains exactly the wrapper div :273 and child anchor :274.
Child :274 has href=/, rel=noopener, and target=_self, which identifies the nested navigation control.
The wrapper has actions=[] and actionBasis={}, with only a pointer-cursor hint.
The screenshot shows Home as a breadcrumb item; classification as container does not classify or authorize its child anchor.

classifications.reason: The visible 4.7 rating score could be passive text or a rating/review entry point. Its one-node subtree and pointer cursor do not establish purpose, so a bounded current-page probe would be required before classifying it as display or interaction.
evidence: The complete subtree contains only a span with class RatingVote_ratingScore__WLmIO and text 4.7.
The node has actions=[] and actionBasis={}.
Its only interaction hint is pointer-cursor, which the classification protocol says is insufficient by itself.
The screenshot places 4.7 beside rating stars but does not reveal whether it opens rating details or merely displays a score.

classifications.reason: This fixed, hittable widget is presented as a chat entry point. Classification as interaction records its likely role but does not create an action or approve opening chat.
evidence: The current node id is ok-cs-button and its complete subtree contains ok-cs-icon, ok-cs-label, and cs-loader-spin children.
The node carries data-hover-label=Chat with us and data-unread-label=New messages.
It is visible with a 52 by 52 rectangle, has a hit target, and appears as the floating support widget in the screenshot.
The node has no supported action basis; therefore this classification alone supplies no dispatch grant.

classifications.reason: The footer candidate aggregates extensive content and many independent links, but its classification subtree is truncated and it also carries a tentative click-handler signal of unknown purpose. The current material cannot safely distinguish a passive landmark/container from a separately actionable footer surface.
evidence: The node is a footer with role contentinfo and spans the complete footer area.
Its captured subtree includes many nested anchors and navigation sections rather than one coherent operation.
classificationBinding.truncated is true, so the protocol forbids a negative display/container conclusion from this material.
The candidate has a tentative click action based only on a handler property whose purpose is unknown.
